ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $D$ and $E$ are points on $AC$ and $BC$, respectively. If $\triangle ADB \cong \triangle EDB \cong \triangle EDC$, what is the measure of $\angle C$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\triangle ADB \cong \triangle EDB \cong \triangle EDC$,\\
it follows that $\angle A = \angle BED = \angle CED$, and $\angle ABD = \angle EBD = \angle C$,\\
since $\angle BED + \angle CED = 180^\circ$,\\
it implies that $\angle A = \angle BED = \angle CED = 90^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle ABD + \angle EBD + \angle C = 90^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle C = \boxed{30^\circ}$.
